title: Media, pubblicità e reclami
sub: Reporting verbs - fake news e reclamo formale
grammar: Reporting verbs e loro costruzioni (suggest, deny, admit, accuse, insist...)
situation: Reclamo formale al telefono e per email

lessons.title: Reporting verbs e loro costruzioni
lessons.intro: Al B2 non basta «he said that». Verbi come deny, admit, accuse, insist, suggest, warn e persuade riassumono in un solo verbo ciò che una persona ha detto o fatto, ma ognuno vuole una costruzione precisa. Ed è lì che gli italiani sbagliano di più.

steps.title: Le cinque costruzioni dei reporting verbs
steps.body:
Il verbo scelto decide che cosa viene dopo:
- **+ that-clause**: admit, claim, complain, explain, insist, point out, suggest, announce, deny: She **insisted that** the figures were correct.
- **+ -ing**: admit, deny, suggest, recommend, regret, mention, propose: He **denied taking** the money. / She **suggested meeting** earlier.
- **+ to-infinitive**: agree, offer, promise, refuse, threaten, claim, demand: They **refused to refund** the ticket.
- **+ oggetto + to-infinitive**: advise, warn, remind, persuade, urge, invite, encourage, order, tell: He **advised me to wait**. / She **warned us not to** click the link.
- **+ oggetto + preposizione + -ing**: accuse sb **of**, blame sb **for**, criticise sb **for**, congratulate sb **on**, thank sb **for**, warn sb **against**: They **accused him of lying**.

Con alcuni verbi si possono usare più costruzioni (admit, claim, deny, suggest): She **admitted making** a mistake / **admitted that** she had made a mistake.

La negazione va davanti al to o all'-ing: **not to** go, **not** going.
ex: The minister denied leaking the documents to the press.
Il ministro ha negato di aver fatto trapelare i documenti alla stampa.
My lawyer advised me not to sign anything.
Il mio avvocato mi ha consigliato di non firmare nulla.
They accused the company of misleading its customers.
Hanno accusato l'azienda di aver ingannato i clienti.
table: He claimed that he was ill.
accuse of, blame for, thank for
He blamed me for the delay.

steps.title: Errori tipici degli italiani
steps.body:
- **say / suggest / explain / describe + me**: in inglese non si dice «She suggested me to go», «He explained me the problem», «Say me the truth».
  - Corretto: She suggested **that I go** / suggested **going**; He explained **the problem to me**; **Tell** me the truth.
- **suggest** non vuole mai il to-infinito: «He suggested to wait» -> He suggested **waiting** / **that we wait**.
- **deny / admit** + to-infinito: «He denied to have taken it» -> He denied **having taken** it / **taking** it.
- **insist** è seguito da **on** + -ing (insist on paying), oppure da that: She insisted that he stay.
- **apologise for** (non «of» né «to» + verbo): I apologise **for being** late.
- **accuse of** (non «to»): They accused him **of** cheating.

Dopo **suggest / insist / demand / recommend** in inglese britannico si usa spesso **should** o la forma base (congiuntivo): She suggested that he **(should) see** a doctor.
ex: She suggested that I check the facts first.
Ha suggerito che io controllassi prima i fatti.
He explained the problem to me.
Mi ha spiegato il problema.
I apologise for being late.
Mi scuso per il ritardo.

steps.title: Forme passive e verbi del discorso indiretto
steps.body:
Nei **testi giornalistici** si usano molto le forme passive impersonali:
- It **is said / believed / reported / thought** that + frase: It is believed that the fire started in the kitchen.
- Soggetto + **is said / believed / alleged to** + infinito: The fire **is believed to have started** in the kitchen. (infinito passato per un fatto anteriore)
- **is reported to be** (stato presente) / **to have been** (stato passato): The minister is reported to be ill.

Ricorda il **backshift** (ma non obbligatorio se il fatto è ancora vero): "I will resign" -> She said she **would** resign. / He announced that he **was** leaving. Nel discorso indiretto cambiano anche pronomi e riferimenti di tempo (today -> that day, tomorrow -> the next day).
ex: The singer is said to have refused the offer.
Si dice che la cantante abbia rifiutato l'offerta.
It is alleged that the company ignored several warnings.
Si sostiene che l'azienda abbia ignorato diversi avvertimenti.

steps.title: Scegliere il verbo giusto: atteggiamento e tono
steps.body:
Il verbo comunica anche **che cosa pensa chi riporta**:
- **say, tell, state, announce**: neutri o ufficiali.
- **claim, allege**: si prendono le distanze: «He claims he was at home» (ma forse non è vero).
- **point out, remind, explain**: informazioni date come vere.
- **admit, confess**: ammissione di qualcosa di negativo.
- **boast, complain, grumble**: tono emotivo.
- **insist, maintain**: si ribadisce con forza.

In un testo B2 evita di ripetere said: un verbo preciso mostra un vocabolario più ricco (criterio Cambridge «language»).
ex: She maintained that she had never seen the document.
Sosteneva di non aver mai visto il documento.
He boasted that he had won every award.
Si vantava di aver vinto tutti i premi.

steps.s: The minister denied ___ the documents to the press.
steps.why: Deny è seguito da -ing (o da that), mai da to + infinito.

steps.s: She accused her manager ___ credit for her idea.
The company has agreed ___ all customers affected by the fault.
My lawyer advised me ___ anything until he arrived.
She insisted ___ paying for the meal.

opts: She suggested that we should check the facts first.
She suggested us to check the facts first.
She suggested to check us the facts first.
steps.why: Suggest non vuole oggetto + to-infinito: si usa that + soggetto (+ should) oppure -ing.

steps.q: Quale frase riporta correttamente «I didn't do it»?
steps.why: Deny + -ing. Refuse vuole to + infinito e ha un altro significato (rifiutare).

steps.s: The council apologised ___ the delay in collecting the rubbish.
She warned us ___ to trust the website: it was a hoax.
The newspaper promised ___ a correction on Monday.
She suggested me to read the report again.
answers: She suggested that I read the report again
She suggested I read the report again
She suggested that I should read the report again
She suggested I should read the report again
She suggested reading the report again
steps.why: Suggest non si usa con oggetto + to-infinito: that + soggetto o -ing.

steps.s: He explained me why the order was late.
answers: He explained to me why the order was late
He explained why the order was late
steps.why: Explain vuole to prima della persona: explain sth to sb.

steps.s: The shop denied to have received the complaint.
answers: The shop denied having received the complaint
The shop denied receiving the complaint
The shop denied that it had received the complaint

steps.s1: "I didn't send the message," he said.
steps.why: Deny + -ing / having + participio per un fatto anteriore.

steps.s1: "You really should see a doctor," Tom said to me.
"I'm sorry I forgot your birthday," she said.
"Let's meet outside the station," said Ben.

steps.it: Ha accusato l'azienda di aver ingannato i clienti.
steps.en: She accused the company of misleading customers

lessons.title: Media, pubblicità e fake news
lessons.intro: Parole per parlare di informazione, pubblicità e notizie false. Servono per leggere gli articoli, scrivere una recensione e fare un reclamo ben argomentato.

ex: The headline was pure clickbait: the article said nothing new.
Il titolo era pura esca per i clic: l'articolo non diceva nulla di nuovo.
Misinformation spread quickly during the election.
Le informazioni false si sono diffuse in fretta durante le elezioni.
words.note: Non numerabile. Disinformation = falsità diffuse di proposito.

ex: We always fact-check our stories before we publish them.
Verifichiamo sempre i fatti prima di pubblicare le notizie.
words.note: Anche nome: a fact-check; chi lo fa è a fact-checker.

ex: The tabloids ran the story on their front pages for a week.
I tabloid hanno tenuto la notizia in prima pagina per una settimana.
words.note: Non è «tabloid» in senso tecnico di formato: indica lo stile sensazionalistico.

ex: The photograph turned out to be an elaborate hoax.
La fotografia si è rivelata una bufala molto elaborata.
The footballer endorses a well-known brand of trainers.
Il calciatore fa da testimonial a una nota marca di scarpe sportive.
The paper had to retract the story and publish an apology.
Il giornale ha dovuto ritrattare la notizia e pubblicare delle scuse.
Their slogan is short, rhythmic and easy to remember.
Il loro slogan è breve, ritmico e facile da ricordare.
The campaign was aimed at a target audience of young parents.
La campagna era rivolta a un pubblico di giovani genitori.
The video went viral within a few hours.
Il video è diventato virale in poche ore.
Only the most gullible readers believed the story.
Solo i lettori più creduloni hanno creduto alla storia.
words.note: Ha tono negativo: non è un complimento.

ex: The report seemed biased in favour of the government.
Il rapporto sembrava di parte a favore del governo.
words.note: Si dice biased towards / against / in favour of.

ex: Several news outlets repeated the claim without checking it.
Diverse testate hanno ripetuto l'affermazione senza verificarla.
The post was sponsored, but nobody had said so.
Il post era sponsorizzato, ma nessuno l'aveva detto.

pairs: fare da testimonial a un prodotto

steps.s: The newspaper was forced to ___ the story after the facts were checked.
The advert's ___ is easy to remember: just four words.
steps.why: Slogan = frase breve e memorabile di una campagna.

steps.s: The report was clearly ___ in favour of one political party.
Journalists must protect their ___ by checking every source.

opts: esagera o stuzzica per spingere a cliccare

steps.s: The video ___ viral within hours of being posted online.
steps.why: Go viral: al passato went viral.

lessons.title: Fake news e titoli esca
lessons.intro: Un articolo su come le notizie false si diffondono e su chi ne è responsabile. Osserva quanti reporting verbs usa l'autore (suggest, admit, deny, argue, criticise, order, advise).

steps.title: The shark on the motorway
steps.text:
Last March, a photograph of a shark swimming along a flooded motorway was shared more than two million times. It was, of course, a fake: the image had been assembled from two unrelated pictures and had first appeared, years earlier, as a joke on a small forum. Nevertheless, several news websites reproduced it, and one regional broadcaster even mentioned it in its evening bulletin before apologising the following morning.

Stories like this are no longer rare. Researchers at a media institute who examined five thousand viral posts discovered that false stories spread roughly six times faster than accurate ones. The explanation, they suggest, is not that people are stupid. It is that invented stories are designed to provoke strong emotions, and strong emotions make us click first and think later. A headline promising a scandal will always travel further than one reporting a budget meeting.

Newspapers themselves are not blameless. Competing for attention with free content, many outlets have adopted what critics call clickbait: headlines that exaggerate or tease in order to attract readers. The editor of one popular website recently admitted that his team routinely rewrites headlines to make them more irresistible, although he denied that this ever involved publishing false information. "We exaggerate the packaging," he said, "not the product." Media analysts are unconvinced. They argue that a misleading headline, read by thousands of people who never open the article, is in effect a false statement.

Advertising has similar problems. A recent campaign for an energy drink claimed to be scientifically proven to improve concentration. The advertising regulator criticised the company for relying on a single study of twelve students and ordered it to withdraw the slogan. Influencers, too, have come under pressure. Several have been accused of endorsing products they had never used, without telling their followers that they were being paid. Since new rules were introduced, they are obliged to state clearly when a post is sponsored.

So what can ordinary readers do? Fact-checking organisations recommend checking the source before sharing anything, looking for the same story in several places, and being especially suspicious of content that makes you angry. They also advise readers to distinguish between a headline and the evidence that is supposed to support it. Some schools have begun teaching these habits to children as young as ten, and early results are encouraging: pupils who took part in a six-week programme were twice as likely to identify a fake image.

Perhaps the most important change, however, would be a cultural one. At present, sharing a story takes one second; correcting a mistake takes days, and the correction is seldom read by anyone who saw the original. Until we start treating the share button with the same care that we give to our spoken words, the shark will keep swimming down the motorway.

qs.q: What does the writer say about the shark photograph?
opts: It was made from two different pictures, but some media used it.
It was a genuine photo from an earlier flood.
It was created by a news website to attract readers.
qs.why: «assembled from two unrelated pictures... several news websites reproduced it»

qs.q: According to researchers, why do false stories spread so fast?
opts: They are designed to trigger strong emotions.
People are not intelligent enough to spot them.
They are more interesting than accurate news.
qs.why: «designed to provoke strong emotions»; i ricercatori dicono che non è questione di stupidità.

qs.q: False stories spread roughly ___ times faster than accurate ones.
What does the website editor deny?
opts: That the website ever publishes false information
qs.why: «he denied that this ever involved publishing false information»

qs.q: What do media analysts think about misleading headlines?
opts: They can be as harmful as a false statement.
They are acceptable if the article is accurate.

qs.q: Why was the energy drink company criticised?
opts: Its claim was based on one small study.
It paid influencers without telling them.
qs.why: «relying on a single study of twelve students»

qs.q: What are influencers now required to do?
opts: Say when a post is paid for
qs.why: «obliged to state clearly when a post is sponsored»

qs.q: What is the writer's main conclusion?
opts: We should be as careful with sharing as with speaking.
qs.why: Ultimo paragrafo: trattare il tasto condividi con la stessa cura delle parole.

steps.q: «Newspapers themselves are not blameless» significa che i giornali:
opts: non sono mai stati accusati di nulla
steps.why: Blameless = senza colpa; con la negazione, «non sono esenti da colpe».

steps.s: Several influencers have come ___ pressure to reveal who is paying them.
steps.why: Come under pressure = essere sottoposti a pressioni (collocazione).

steps.s: A deliberately ___ headline can easily mislead readers.
steps.why: Participio con funzione di aggettivo: exaggerated.
In effect = in pratica, nella realtà.

lessons.title: Un reclamo al telefono
lessons.intro: Una cliente telefona al servizio clienti per un ordine danneggiato. Ascolta come si espone un reclamo formale e come risponde l'operatore.

steps.title: A formal complaint
steps.it: Ascolta la telefonata. Puoi riascoltarla e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Good morning, Brightside Electrics, you are speaking to Daniel. How can I help?
Good morning. My name is Laura Bennett, and I am calling to make a formal complaint about an order, number 40718.
I am sorry to hear that, Ms Bennett. Could you tell me what happened?

I ordered a washing machine on the third of May. You promised delivery within five working days. It arrived on the nineteenth, and when the delivery men unpacked it, there was a large dent in the side.
I do apologise. Did the drivers note the damage on the delivery form?
No. They insisted that the dent had been there when it left the warehouse, and that it was not their responsibility, but they refused to take it back.
I see. And have you contacted us about this before?

Yes. I rang last Tuesday and spoke to a colleague of yours. He admitted that the machine was damaged and said someone would call me back within two days. Nobody did. I then emailed on Friday, and I still have not had a reply.
That is not the standard we aim for. May I ask what outcome you would like?
I would like a full refund, including the delivery charge, which was forty-five pounds. Alternatively, a replacement delivered by the end of next week, but I am no longer sure I trust the company.

Understandably. Let me check the system. I can see your email, and you are right, it has not been answered. I am going to pass this to a senior manager, who will contact you within twenty-four hours. If you have not heard by Thursday at noon, please ring this number again and quote the reference.
It is C, W, seven, two, three. I will also email you to confirm everything we have discussed.
Thank you. I would also like you to know that if this is not settled, I am going to take it to the consumer ombudsman.
I understand, Ms Bennett, and I can only apologise again.

qs.q: What is wrong with the washing machine?
What went wrong with the delivery date?
opts: The machine arrived later than promised.
The delivery men came on the wrong day.

qs.q: How did the delivery men react?
opts: They said the damage was not their responsibility and would not take the machine back.
They noted the damage on the form.

qs.q: What did the colleague promise on the phone?
opts: That someone would call her back within two days
That she would receive a refund
That a replacement would be sent
A senior manager will contact her within twenty-four hours.
She will receive a refund today.
The delivery men will return tomorrow.

qs.q: What does Ms Bennett say she will do if the problem is not solved?
opts: Take it to the consumer ombudsman

steps.en: They insisted that the dent had been there when it left the warehouse.
steps.it: Hanno insistito che l'ammaccatura c'era già quando è uscita dal magazzino.

steps.en: He admitted that the machine was damaged.
steps.it: Ha ammesso che la macchina era danneggiata.

steps.en: I am calling to make a formal complaint about an order.
steps.it: Chiamo per presentare un reclamo formale riguardo a un ordine.

lessons.title: Reclamo formale al telefono e per email
lessons.intro: Esporre il problema, dire che cosa ti aspetti e restare fermo senza essere maleducato. Le frasi giuste fanno la differenza tra essere ascoltati e essere liquidati.

steps.title: Il reclamo al telefono
steps.body:
- **Presentarsi**: I'm calling about order number... / I'd like to make a formal complaint about...
- **Spiegare**: The problem is that... / When it arrived, it was... / I was told that...
- **Riferire ciò che è stato detto**: He promised to call me back, but nobody did. / They insisted that it wasn't their fault.
- **Chiedere una soluzione**: I would like a full refund. / I expect the matter to be resolved by...
- **Restare fermi ma cortesi**: I appreciate your help, but that isn't acceptable. / I'm afraid that doesn't solve the problem.
- **Minacciare con garbo**: If it isn't resolved, I will have to take it further.

Tono: calmo, preciso (date, numeri d'ordine), mai insulti. Chiedi sempre un **riferimento** e il nome dell'operatore.
ex: I would like to make a formal complaint about an order.
Vorrei presentare un reclamo formale riguardo a un ordine.
I was told that someone would call me back within two days.
Mi era stato detto che qualcuno mi avrebbe richiamato entro due giorni.

steps.title: Il reclamo scritto
steps.body:
- **Apertura**: I am writing to complain about... / I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with...
- **Fatti**: On 3 May I ordered... The goods arrived on... but...
- **Richiesta**: I would be grateful if you could refund... / I expect a full refund within 14 days.
- **Chiusura**: I look forward to hearing from you. Yours sincerely / Yours faithfully.

Registro formale: niente contrazioni, niente slang. Usa i **reporting verbs** per i fatti: Your representative **assured** me that..., **promised to**..., **refused to**...

Errore tipico: «I want that you refund me»: in inglese si dice **I would like you to refund me** / **I would be grateful if you could**.
ex: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with the service I received.
Le scrivo per esprimere la mia insoddisfazione per il servizio ricevuto.
I would be grateful if you could refund the full amount.
Le sarei grato se potesse rimborsare l'intero importo.

steps.title: Reclamo per un hotel
steps.it: Sei al telefono con la direzione di un hotel. Scegli le risposte più adatte (Tu).
lines: Good evening, Riverside Hotel, Mark Davies speaking.

opts: Good evening. I would like to make a complaint about the room I was given last night.
Good evening. I want that you change me the room.
Good evening. Your hotel is the worst I have ever seen.

lines: I am sorry to hear that. What was the problem?

opts: The receptionist assured me that the room had a view of the river, but it faces the car park, and the air conditioning did not work.
The receptionist has said me that the room has a view of the river, but it looks to the car park.

lines: I do apologise. What would you like us to do?

opts: I would like a partial refund, and I would appreciate it if you could confirm that in writing.
I want to have back the half of the money immediately.

steps.title: Il rimborso viene rifiutato
steps.it: L'operatore rifiuta il rimborso. Scegli le risposte migliori (Tu).
lines: Unfortunately, our policy doesn't allow refunds after thirty days.

opts: I understand that, but I contacted you within a week, and your colleague promised to look into it.
I understand that, but your colleague has promised to look at it me.
Your policy is stupid and I will never buy from you again.

lines: I see. I can offer you a voucher instead.

opts: I'm afraid a voucher doesn't solve the problem. I would like to speak to a manager, please.
I'm afraid a voucher it doesn't solve the problem. I want a manager now.
Fine, whatever. Give me the voucher.

lines: Certainly. I'll pass you to my manager.

opts: Thank you. Could I also have the reference number for this complaint?
Thank you. Can you say me the reference number?
Thanks. I will remember everything you said.

pairs: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with...
Le scrivo per esprimere la mia insoddisfazione per...
I would be grateful if you could...
I expect the matter to be resolved.
Mi aspetto che la questione sia risolta.
He refused to take it back.
I would like to speak to a manager.

steps.it: Mi hanno assicurato che avrebbero richiamato entro due giorni.
steps.en: They assured me that they would call back within two days
steps.why: Assure sb that + frase al condizionale (backshift di will).

steps.en: I would like to make a formal complaint about an order.
steps.it: Vorrei presentare un reclamo formale riguardo a un ordine.

steps.en: I was told that someone would call me back within two days.
steps.it: Mi era stato detto che qualcuno mi avrebbe richiamato entro due giorni.

steps.en: I would like to speak to a manager, please.
steps.it: Vorrei parlare con un responsabile, per favore.

steps.q: Imagine that a hotel room or a product did not match what was promised. Make a complaint by phone.
steps.it: Telefona per fare un reclamo (almeno 6 frasi): presentati, descrivi il problema con almeno due reporting verbs, chiedi una soluzione.
steps.model: Good morning. I am calling to make a formal complaint about a laptop I bought from your website on the second of June. The salesman assured me that it came with a two-year guarantee, but the receipt says only twelve months. When I rang your helpline, a colleague of yours denied that the guarantee had ever been mentioned, and he refused to put anything in writing. I would like you to check the original advertisement and confirm the correct terms. If that is not possible, I would like a full refund. I look forward to hearing from you within the next two days.

lessons.title: La recensione (B2 First Part 2)
lessons.intro: Scrivere una recensione efficace: opinione chiara, descrizione, punti forti e deboli, raccomandazione. Poi parla di pubblicità e informazione.

steps.title: Come si scrive una recensione
steps.body:
Struttura in 4 parti (una per paragrafo):
1. **Titolo e apertura**: presenta ciò che recensisci e dai subito la tua idea generale: Last month I watched..., which I would recommend to anyone who...
2. **Descrizione**: di che cosa tratta, chi è il protagonista, come si sviluppa: The film follows... / The author sets out to show that...
3. **Valutazione**: punti forti e punti deboli: Its greatest strength is... / However, the second half is less convincing. / On the downside, ...
4. **Raccomandazione**: Despite..., it is well worth watching. / I would not recommend it to anyone who...

Lessico utile: gripping, thought-provoking, well-paced, predictable, overrated, a must-see. Usa i **reporting verbs** per riferire le tesi: The director **claims / argues / insists** that...

Criteri Cambridge: **contenuto** (rispondi a tutti i punti della traccia), **comunicazione** (tono adatto ai lettori, opinione chiara), **organizzazione** (paragrafi e connettivi: However, In addition, Despite this), **lingua** (varietà di lessico e strutture, pochi errori).
ex: Its greatest strength is the way it mixes interviews with striking graphics.
Il suo punto di forza è il modo in cui mescola interviste e grafica efficace.
The director insists that social media companies could stop misinformation tomorrow.
La regista sostiene con forza che i social media potrebbero fermare la disinformazione domani.

steps.q: Quale frase è adatta alla conclusione di una recensione?
opts: Despite its weaknesses, it is well worth watching.
Finally I want to say goodbye to everybody.
That is all I know about the film.
steps.why: La conclusione dà una raccomandazione motivata, con un connettivo di contrasto.

steps.s1: The director says that the film is based on a true story.
steps.s2: The director ___ based on a true story.
steps.why: Claim + that-clause; the key word deve restare invariata.

steps.s: The plot is rather ___ : you can guess the ending after ten minutes.
The film is thought to be made in Iceland in 2018.
answers: The film is thought to have been made in Iceland in 2018
It is thought that the film was made in Iceland in 2018
steps.why: Per un fatto passato si usa l'infinito passato: to have been made.

steps.q: You have recently watched a documentary about social media and misinformation. Your English-language magazine has asked readers to send in reviews. Write your review. Say what the documentary is about, what you liked and disliked, and whether you would recommend it.
steps.it: Scrivi una recensione (140-190 parole) con titolo, descrizione, punti forti e deboli e raccomandazione. Usa almeno due reporting verbs (claim, argue, insist, admit...) e lessico dell'unità.
checklist: Contenuto: ho detto di che cosa parla il documentario, che cosa mi è piaciuto, che cosa no e se lo raccomando
Comunicazione: ho dato un'opinione chiara con un tono adatto ai lettori di una rivista
Organizzazione: ho scritto un titolo e paragrafi distinti, con connettivi (However, In addition, Despite...)
Lingua: ho usato almeno due reporting verbs con la costruzione corretta
Lingua: ho usato lessico vario (misinformation, hoax, biased, gripping...) evitando ripetizioni
Ho controllato spelling UK e punteggiatura
useful: Last month I watched..., which I would recommend to anyone who...
However, the second half is less convincing.
steps.model:
The Truth Machine: a documentary worth watching

Last month I watched The Truth Machine, a ninety-minute documentary about how false stories spread online, and I would recommend it to anyone who has ever shared a headline without reading the article.

The film follows a young fact-checker, Lena Ortiz, who traces a hoax about a poisoned water supply back to its source: a bored teenager with a free weekend. Lena admits that she was shocked, and the film does not pretend that the problem is simple. Its greatest strength is the way it mixes interviews with striking graphics, which makes complicated data easy to follow.

However, the second half is less convincing. The director insists that social media companies could stop misinformation tomorrow, yet she offers little evidence for this claim. In addition, the music is sometimes so dramatic that it feels manipulative, which is ironic in a film about honesty.

Despite these weaknesses, the documentary is informative and entertaining. It will make you think twice before you press the share button.

steps.q: Describe an advertisement or a campaign that you remember. Why was it effective?
steps.it: Descrivi una pubblicità o una campagna che ricordi (almeno 6 frasi): pubblico, slogan, perché funziona.
steps.model: I remember an advert for a mineral water brand. It was aimed at young people who do a lot of sport, and its slogan was only three words long, which made it easy to remember. The advert claimed that the water came from a mountain spring, and it showed a runner drinking it at the top of a hill. I think it worked because the images were beautiful and the message was simple. Personally, I was a little sceptical about the claim, but I still bought the water for a while.

steps.q: How do you check whether a piece of news is true? Have you ever been fooled by fake news?
steps.it: Racconta come verifichi le notizie ed eventualmente un caso in cui sei stato ingannato (almeno 6 frasi).
hints: It turned out to be a hoax.
steps.model: Before I share something, I usually look for the same story on at least two different websites. I also check who has published it, because some outlets are clearly biased. I once read that a famous actor had died, and I immediately sent the news to my friends. It turned out to be a hoax, and I felt rather foolish. Now I always read the whole article, and I never trust a headline that makes me angry.

lessons.title: Test dell'unità 6 (B2)
lessons.intro: Verifica senza aiuti: reporting verbs, lessico dei media, reclamo formale, un cloze e un ascolto.

steps.s: The minister denied ___ the documents to the press.
They accused the company ___ misleading its customers.
The airline refused ___ the passengers for the delay.
Our teacher reminded us ___ our passports to the exam.
steps.why: Remind sb to + infinito: ricordare a qualcuno di fare qualcosa. («that we bring» non è naturale qui).

steps.s: She insisted ___ speaking to the manager.
The newspaper had to ___ its story after the mistake was discovered.
The advertising regulator criticised the company ___ using a misleading slogan.
The report was so ___ that nobody trusted it.
The journalist's ___ was damaged after the false story.

steps.title: Completa la risposta con una parola per spazio
steps.text:
Dear Mr Hill,

Thank you for your email. I apologise {1} the delay in replying. You accuse us {2} ignoring your first message, and I admit that we should have answered sooner. However, I must point {3} that our records show we replied on 3 May. The manager has agreed {4} refund the full amount, and she has asked me {5} tell you that a cheque will be sent within a week.

Yours sincerely,
Paula Grey

steps.s1: "You must not touch the cables," the technician said to us.
"It wasn't me who broke the vase," said Tom.
"I'll definitely pay by Friday," he said.

steps.s: She insisted to pay for the dinner.
answers: She insisted on paying for the dinner
She insisted that she would pay for the dinner
She insisted she would pay for the dinner
She insisted that she should pay for the dinner

steps.s: He suggested me a better hotel.
answers: He suggested a better hotel to me
He suggested to me a better hotel
steps.why: Suggest non ammette la persona subito dopo il verbo: suggest sth to sb.

steps.q: Quale frase indica che chi riporta prende le distanze da ciò che dice un altro?
opts: He claims he was at home.
He points out he was at home.
He reminds us he was at home.
steps.why: Claim segnala dubbio; point out e remind presentano un fatto come vero.

steps.q: Quale frase è adatta a un reclamo formale scritto?
opts: I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with the service I received.
I want to tell you that your service is rubbish.
I wanna complain about your awful service.

steps.why: Hoax = notizia o scherzo inventato per ingannare.

steps.it: Ci ha consigliato di non fidarci del sito.
steps.en: She advised us not to trust the website

steps.title: A message from customer service
lines: Good afternoon, Ms Bennett. This is Daniel from Brightside Electrics. I am calling to say that our manager has agreed to refund the full price of the washing machine, including the delivery charge. You will receive the money within five working days. I would also like to apologise again for the delay in dealing with your complaint. If you have any questions, please quote the reference, C W seven two three, when you call us.

qs.q: What has the manager agreed to do?
opts: Refund the full price and delivery charge
